worked_solution:
For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=16$ and $\phi =\frac{\theta }{2}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})]}^{16} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(16\cdot \frac{\theta }{2})-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(16\cdot \frac{\theta }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
